To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) tDCS has no effect on cognition in healthy participants, 2) the effect of tDCS is not dependent on stimulation intensity and 3) the effect of active stimulation is not dependent on the effect of sham stimulation.
(1) tDCS does not have a significant effect on healthy subjects’ cognitive function, (2) tDCS may be beneficial for patients with brain diseases.

a) The effect size (Hedge’s g) of single-session transcranially delivered tDCS in healthy subjects is 0.11, and b) the effect size of single-session tDCS is 0.21 in studies with sham stimulation control.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of stimulation on the outcome.
the effects of active (and sham) stimulation, not the post-active (or post-sham) scores.
the effects of tDCS on cognitive functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tDCS has no cognitive effect in healthy subjects.
single-session tDCS has no significant cognitive effect on healthy population.
single-session tDCS has no cognitive effect in the majority of healthy populations based on meta-analysis of 59 studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cognitive effect from single session of tDCS is not clear.
single-session tDCS has no significant cognitive effect in healthy subjects.
tDCS does not affect cognitive function in healthy individuals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to consider the effect of stimulation on the cognitive performance of healthy subjects in the context of a sham-controlled study design.
it is not appropriate to use post-active or postsham stimulation outcome scores to calculate the summary effect size.
tDCS has no cognitive effect.
